task_specification.objective: Advance release convergence through three bounded families: authored-cemetery spatial repair, deterministic wave/Bellkeeper and upgrade-choice progression, and isolated dense-profile qualification readiness.

diagnosis.root_cause: The authored cemetery package remains bound, but landmark visibility and collision alignment are not fully demonstrated during ordinary traversal. Wave/director/boss progression and dense-profile qualification are separate failed release gates.

stop_conditions: Preserve the intact authored cemetery package; do not split, duplicate, hide, reposition, or surgically edit authored child meshes.
Do not replace native streets with proxy floors or generated road patches.
Do not claim dense native-renderer qualification when only software-renderer evidence is available.
Leave runtime recapture, formal verdicts, issue closure, and phase closure to GameLoop Runtime and Tester.

strategy.rationale: Use additive transform-space world binding, authoritative run-state progression, and isolated performance instrumentation as three distinct root-cause strategies. This changes prior camera-only/evidence-recovery treatment while preserving the accepted authored package and native project baseline.

code: Run focused Godot/script checks for cemetery loading, transform-space collision/navigation binding, landmark and perimeter anchors, wave and Bellkeeper transitions, upgrade projection/application, restart reset, and dense-profile setup/teardown.
Verify no forbidden authored-map surgery, duplicate environment, proxy floor, release-visible tester_* action, or unguarded instrumentation is introduced.
Run static checks for authoritative state ownership, spawn safety, input routing, truthful upgrade deltas, and release guards.
runtime: GameLoop Runtime recaptures four cardinal interior-street views, spawn-to-route movement replay, landmark before/near/after traversal, perimeter collision/visibility, and yaw/pitch probes with paired runtime_state and distinct screenshots.
GameLoop Runtime and Tester recapture ordinary waves, composition changes, elite pressure, Bellkeeper arrival/phases/defeat or failure, Result, upgrade-draft focus/selection, and clean Retry.

Tester executes dense prepare/advance/reset and evaluates frame-time distribution, entity/projectile bounds, collector readiness, and three-cycle reset isolation; native renderer status remains host-owned.
visual: Compare shipped gameplay views with the bound Mournlight reference for coherent cemetery scale, external depth, grounded streets, readable landmarks, escape lanes, and no disappearance/occlusion drift.

Inspect the upgrade page at native viewport and supported UI scales for visual hierarchy, silhouettes or icons, current-to-new values, no more than three decision-relevant stat deltas, restrained copy, and keyboard, mouse, and gamepad focus states.
Confirm HUD and full-screen overlays do not capture movement probes or obscure the central arena; treat dense telemetry as supporting evidence only.

done_when: The intact authored cemetery is the sole visual environment, supplemented only by an outer datum and additive collision, navigation, spawn, objective, and boundary anchors.
The arena has larger traversable scale, coherent external world/external depth, and readable keeper post, central building/landmark, cracked bell, escape lanes, and perimeter/boundary.

Collision agrees with rendered landmark footprints and the perimeter; ordinary movement or movement replay around landmark sides and along the boundary cannot pass through, leave the arena, or cause disappearance/occlusion.

Four cardinal first-person diagnostic views from an interior native street show stable landmarks and ground contact; horizontal mouse motion changes yaw and camera_forward, vertical motion changes pitch, and full-screen HUD mouse_filter does not intercept either probe.
Tester has a same-loop black-box and white-box retest covering spawn, critical route, central building/landmark, perimeter/boundary, collision, disappearance/occlusion, and ordinary movement.
tasks.instructions: Inspect the real cemetery scene, authored package transform, camera/framing, collision/navigation owners, spawn/objective anchors, and UI input routing. Rebase additive bindings onto native authored streets and bind landmark/perimeter collision to rendered bounds. Preserve the package while delivering larger traversable scale, external depth, escape lanes, and stable landmark sightlines. Define runtime screenshot/state matrices for spawn, route, before/near/after landmark traversal, perimeter, and mouse yaw/pitch probes.
tasks.title: Restore authored cemetery scale, landmarks, collision, and traversal

done_when: The director advances through five escalating waves with changing archetype composition, elite pressure, live-cap/spawn-budget enforcement, and no spawning after victory or failure; authoritative state exposes wave and director phase and resets cleanly.

The Bellkeeper transition is reachable on the final-wave threshold, presents distinct telegraphs and boss health, executes two readable phases with summon or lane pressure and a recovery window, and resolves exactly once into victory/failure and Result.
Automatic combat remains survivor-like; wave and boss transitions require no hidden tester-only release action; Retry starts a clean run.

The level-up page uses a clear visual hierarchy with weapon or upgrade silhouettes or icons, compact stat icons, truthful current-to-new values, no more than three decision-relevant stat deltas, no NEW or LOCKED placeholder in the CURRENT column, restrained copy, and complete keyboard, mouse, and gamepad focus states.

Selecting a card applies the authoritative id/rank/modifier before gameplay resumes, debounces held confirm, and exposes the selected build in runtime state; Tester can replay waves, boss outcome, draft selection, Result, and Retry.
tasks.instructions: Trace and repair the authoritative run controller, wave director, encounter spawner, Bellkeeper actor, terminal/restart transitions, and the real upgrade-draft scene/controller. Implement deterministic pacing, safe spawns, explicit boss phases, and exactly-once terminal results. Give the upgrade page a visual hierarchy with silhouettes or icons, truthful current-to-new values, no more than three decision-relevant stat deltas, and keyboard, mouse, and gamepad focus. Keep release behavior player-facing and data-driven; add only bounded diagnostics for wave, director phase, boss phase, terminal reason, offered upgrade, and selected upgrade.
tasks.title: Complete wave, Bellkeeper, and upgrade-choice progression

done_when: A release-guarded dense-profile mode deterministically drives a high-entity final-wave/boss scenario through authoritative gameplay APIs and preserves normal lifecycle reset.

Instrumentation records bounded frame/update timings, active enemies, projectiles, pickups, and collector readiness without changing gameplay semantics or substituting for native-renderer qualification.

Start, sample, stop, and reset complete without runtime errors, unbounded allocations, stale actors, duplicate callbacks, or persistent pause; each operation emits requested/resolved/setup-generation/reset-isolation receipts.
Tester can execute the profile against the frozen dense contract while any llvmpipe/native-renderer limitation remains explicitly host-owned.
tasks.instructions: Repair the candidate-owned dense qualification path with isolated setup/teardown, deterministic high-entity driving, bounded telemetry, collector readiness, and release-build guards. Keep instrumentation non-invasive and separate from gameplay truth; never fabricate samples or treat counters as a native renderer verdict. Expose serial tester_dense_prepare, tester_dense_advance, and tester_dense_reset receipts for host recapture.
